checks.name: Both actual entrypoints start against one isolated Firestore project
Two students register and log in; finance admin logs in through actual HTTP routes
Lectura inicial de Mi plan devuelve cuenta gratis, catálogo, cuota y hora de reinicio
Checkout is created through the full application without granting a paid right
Al volver con el pago pendiente, consultar estado, catálogo y cuota conserva la sesión y el plan gratuito
Signed webhook enters the real app and persists one financial entitlement
Student and finance admin read matching subscription, owner, amount and period
Las lecturas de retorno confirmado conservan la suscripción y la cuota ilimitada
Repeating the confirmed event preserves the same financial projection
The other logged-in student sees no purchased subscription, invoice or foreign Checkout
Supplied backend sources and dependency locks remain byte-identical

limitations: Two supplied backend entrypoints and their current local identity are exercised; no implementation from another group is included.
Stripe SDK uses a synthetic loopback HTTP provider. No remote Stripe sandbox, card network or actual charges are tested.
Firestore Emulator only; cloud IAM/rules/indexes and operational deployment are not validated.
HTTP registration/login use temporary synthetic accounts; phone verification is disabled only in the isolated test environment.
No browser or hosted Checkout page is used; CORS preflight, refresh-cookie roundtrip, UI rendering and navigation are not certified.
HTTP requests use loopback. The unchanged administrator entrypoint binds to its default interfaces rather than honoring HOST.
Financial snapshots contain a documented field selection, not whole Firestore documents or authentication/session stores.
This single financial journey contains multiple checkpoints; they are not independent complete acceptance scenarios.
The selected backend is exercised locally. Browser interactions, Docker, deployment and external integration are outside this HTTP run.
